intro_html: Kalua pork is Hawaiian comfort food at its simplest: pork, cabbage, and a long slow cook. This is a genuinely cheap bowl at just $1.90 a serving (at everyday cost), and it still delivers 56 grams of protein. Fourteen servings from a short ingredient list is proof that good food does not have to be complicated.
cost_closing_html: About $1.90 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Every serving comes in around 567 calories with 56 grams of protein.
upsell_html: Three ingredients, about $1.90 a bowl (at everyday cost), and it tastes like the islands. Hard to argue with that. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: This recipe wins on a short ingredient list. Just pork, rice, and cabbage means fewer things to buy and less to go wrong.
Green cabbage is one of the best deals in the produce aisle at under 70 cents a pound, and it cooks down soft and savory.
Season with plain salt and let the slow cooker do the rest. There is no need for fancy spice blends here.
make_it: Set the pork loin in the slow cooker and season it well with salt.
Add a splash of water, cover, and cook on low for 8 to 9 hours until it falls apart.
Shred the pork right in the pot and stir it through the juices.
Pile the chopped cabbage on top of the pork.
Cover and cook another 30 to 45 minutes until the cabbage is tender.
Serve the pork and cabbage over cooked white rice and portion out.
